items.title: Three structural properties of the stability relation: intersecting chords, unstable chords, and invariant blocks
items.author: Avichai Marmor
items.work: Schur-positivity of short chords in matchings
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `lem:properties of core` at source lines 873-881: intersecting chords are stable, a chord is stable if and only if some intermediate vertex is stable, and a perfect non-crossing restriction to an invariant block consists entirely of unstable chords. The author's proof (source lines 883-893) treats the three parts separately and the third is not a formality: after using the definition of invariance to pair each vertex of the block with another vertex of the block (line 889), it restricts the matching to the stable vertices of the block and observes that this restricted matching is short-chord-free, non-crossing and perfect, so it must be the empty matching (line 890). The first two parts are argued by tracking what can be removed: crossing chords cannot be removed one without the other (line 885), and instability of a chord is equivalent to all inner vertices being unstable (lines 886-887).
